headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channels or write/network capabilities, but B can process audio files while A is a docs-only LlamaFactory wrapper.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or network surfaces, and B likewise has no shared channel with A. With no documented bridge between LlamaFactory and whisper, prompt injection via one agent’s outputs into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects A outputs to B inputs through a shared channel, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent is wrapped with a copy-paste or message-queue bridge, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or queue.
Do not pipe A output directly into B prompts.
Review any wrapper code for hidden message passing.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no file or network egress; B touches audio/speech and can read audio files, but neither profile shows a shared workspace or outbound transmission. The only plausible leakage path is an unusual external file handoff, so blast radius is small and not default.
conditions: IF A and B are placed in the same shared directory, leakage risk increases.
IF audio files contain sensitive speech and are copied between agents, data exposure becomes possible.
mitigations: Store A and B in separate workspaces.
Avoid placing sensitive audio in shared folders.
Delete transient audio files after use.
Restrict file permissions on any handoff directory.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP, so there is no overlapping mutable resource to contend over. B also cannot run multiple instances, but that does not create a conflict with A because A is non-runnable and write-disabled.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory, reassess for conflict.
IF an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state, locking may be needed.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not mount a shared writable volume.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same artifacts.
requires-engineering: add locks if write access is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a fine-tuning toolkit and B is a speech model; the profiles do not show that B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative, nor that either agent can take downstream actions. Any cascade would require an external workflow to treat A’s generated artifacts as trusted input to B, which is not default here.
conditions: IF an operator feeds A-generated text into B as instructions, cascading errors become possible.
IF B is used to act on A-produced transcripts without review, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Use schema validation on A outputs before reuse.
Keep B limited to transcription, not decision-making.
Document that A outputs are untrusted inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: A is docs-only and touches no data classes, while B touches audio/speech and audio files. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling of audio content rather than a specific cross-agent violation. The other agent is not cited for a residency issue because none is shown.
conditions: IF audio files include regulated content and are routed to a noncompliant environment, compliance risk increases.
IF retention policies differ across the storage path, reassess.
mitigations: Classify audio before processing.
Keep regulated audio out of shared storage.
Set a short deletion schedule for temporary files.
Confirm local policy for speech data handling.
